summary: Verified P1 PII-redaction fix for export endpoints. Seeded two signed-off TEST_PII_EXPORT_* meetings (one with pii_redactions targeting 'Demo Manager'/'Demo User' -> [Redacted], one with []). Hit all 6 export endpoints (review.py: export-pdf, export-transcript; admin.py: export-evidence [PDF+CSV], export-cqc-excerpts, export-cc-excerpts, export-transcripts), extracted PDF text with pypdf, and asserted (a) raw attendee/manager names ABSENT + [Redacted] PRESENT for redacted meeting, (b) raw names PRESENT for the no-redaction regression meeting. All 12 test cases pass. No 500s, all correct content-types (application/pdf, text/csv).
critical_code_review_comments: Redaction is applied consistently via apply_redactions_deep/apply_redactions_to_text on a shallow-copied meeting dict (mtg_for_pdf / pdf_meeting / attendee_list) in all 6 endpoints — the raw mtg/meeting dict is preserved so the original DB row isn't mutated in memory. Good pattern.
admin.export-evidence CSV: staff_name is pulled from mtg_for_pdf.attendees (the redacted list), so CSV 'Staff Member' column is redacted correctly. Verified.

admin.export-cc-excerpts: correctly redacts the 'attendees' metadata line via _apply_redactions_deep(include, redactions) but the separate staff_label built from /users when staff_ids filter is passed is (intentionally) NOT redacted — matches the review-request spec.

Minor: no unit test for the case where a redaction 'original' partially overlaps a name (e.g. only first name). Existing implementation handles this via case-insensitive substring regex — could be worth an explicit test in future.
